13. If the mapping uses cardinality as a metric, then it must be clearly defined in terms of what is being linked between source and target, how the cardinalities are counted, and the direction of the map. The cardinality of a map (one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one, and many-to-many), without a clear definition, however, has a very weak semantic definition, being nothing more than the numbers of source entities and target entities that are linked in the map. 14. Maps should be machine-readable to optimize their utility. 15. When creating maps using ICD-11, map into the foundation component first, then generate maps to mortality and morbidity statistics through linearization aggregation.
